summary: One option inside a RadioGroup. Meaningless on its own — the group owns the name and the selected value.

useInstead.when: the user may pick more than one
there are more than about five options
useInstead.why: a long radio list costs vertical space no one reads

neutral.use: a choice with no positive reading — sort order, display mode

guarantees: `name` and the selected value come from the group's context, so no Radio has to repeat them

antiPatterns.why: it has no name and no siblings, so it can be selected but never unselected
the group owns selection; per-option wiring is what the context exists to remove
a single radio cannot be cleared once chosen — that is a Checkbox
